answer: Keep your car insured until the sale is complete and the car is in our hands, including on the day of a home pickup, and cancel your policy or remove the car from it only after you sign the paperwork; ask your insurer about a refund for the unused part of your premium. Before you hand over the car, remove toll tags and parking stickers, clear garage door codes, unpair your phone, and remove the car from any connected-car app account. What to do with your plates depends on the state that issued them, not where you live: North Carolina plates stay on the car, Virginia, Georgia and Texas plates should be removed and kept, and California plates must be returned to California within 10 days using the receipt we give you (form NW-PLT-1). If your car is registered in a state other than North Carolina, it needs an emissions certificate from a North Carolina inspection station before we can buy it at a North Carolina store.
